subtopics.title: FIDE, the global chess body
subtopics.summary: FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), the International Chess Federation, is the global governing authority for chess. Founded in Paris in 1924, it oversees major international competitions and sets rules and rating standards. Its headquarters is in Lausanne, Switzerland, and Arkady Dvorkovich is its President.
facts: Full name: Fédération Internationale des Échecs (International Chess Federation)
Established in Paris in 1924
Headquarters: Lausanne, Switzerland
Serves as the global governing authority for chess
Oversees all major international competitions
Sets rules and rating standards
President: Arkady Dvorkovich
Deputy President: Viswanathan Anand
Motto: Gens una Sumus (We are One Family)
International Chess Day on 20 July marks FIDE's foundation; 2025 theme 'Every Move Counts'

subtopics.title: Chess history and records
subtopics.summary: Chess has a long history, from its origin as 'Chaturanga' in Northern India during the Gupta Empire to the World Chess Championship, first contested in 1886. Recent events include India hosting the Chess World Cup 2025 in Goa and India's first-ever Olympiad gold in 2024. Several records involve very young players and wins over Magnus Carlsen.
facts: World Chess Championship established in 1886; Wilhelm Steinitz became the 1st official champion
Chess originated in Northern India during the Gupta Empire (6th century CE) as 'Chaturanga'
India hosted the Chess World Cup 2025 in Goa, its second time after Hyderabad in 2002
Javokhir Sindarov (Uzbek) won the Chess World Cup 2025
Indian men's and women's teams won their first-ever gold at the 45th Chess Olympiad in Budapest, Hungary, in 2024
R. Praggnanandhaa became the youngest player to reach a World Cup final, and only the 2nd Indian after Viswanathan Anand to do so
Gukesh Dommaraju secured his first classical win over Magnus Carlsen at Norway Chess 2025
R. Praggnanandhaa was the first Indian to defeat Magnus Carlsen in classical chess
Abhimanyu Mishra (USA) holds the record as the world's youngest chess Grandmaster
Anish Sarkar, aged 3 and from Kolkata, became the youngest chess player ever ranked by FIDE
